ask: Write the doctype declaration for a modern HTML page.
why: Without it the browser uses 1990s quirks mode and your spacing shifts.

ask: Open the root element and declare the page language as English.
why: lang tells a screen reader how to pronounce the words.

ask: Write a head section containing only the character set declaration.
why: Without charset, a rupee sign or an accented name turns to junk.

ask: Add the viewport meta tag that makes a page work on phones.
why: Miss it and phones render a shrunken 980px desktop layout.

ask: Give the page the title 'CSE326 Notes'.
why: The title is the browser tab AND the blue headline in search results.

ask: Link an external stylesheet called style.css.
why: link is an empty element - it never gets a closing tag.

ask: Link an external JavaScript file called app.js.

checks.label: script is closed
checks.hint: script always needs a closing </script>, even with src.

why: Unlike link, script is NOT an empty element.

ask: Write a main page heading that says 'Welcome'.
why: One h1 per page - it is the page's single subject.

ask: Write a heading hierarchy: a main title, a section, and a sub-section beneath it.
why: Screen readers build a table of contents from these levels.

ask: Write two separate paragraphs.
why: Two ideas means two paragraphs, never a double line break.

ask: Write a three-line postal address inside ONE paragraph.
solution:
School of Computer Science
Block 34
Phagwara
why: An address is one idea printed over several lines - that is br's job.

ask: Add a thematic break between two paragraphs.
why: hr means the subject changes; drawing a line is a side effect.

ask: Wrap a few words mid-sentence in a generic inline container.
why: span is inline - it does not break the line.

ask: Create a generic block container with the class 'box'.
why: div is a block with no meaning - prefer a semantic element when one fits.

ask: Mark the word 'Warning' as genuinely IMPORTANT (semantic, not just bold).
why: strong carries importance; <b> only makes it look bold.

ask: Emphasise the word 'never' so the sentence's meaning changes.
why: em changes how a screen reader delivers the sentence.

ask: Make a keyword visually bold WITHOUT implying importance.
why: b draws the eye. strong says it matters. Exams test the difference.

ask: Mark a species name in italics as a different KIND of text.
why: i is for a different kind of text, not for emphasis.

ask: Highlight the word 'Monday' as if with a marker pen.
Show an old price struck through and a new price inserted.
Write the chemical formula for water and the area of a square.
Add a legal disclaimer in small print.
Mark up the abbreviation HTML with its full form.

checks.label: abbr has title
checks.hint: Add title="..." with the full form.

ask: Write a SHORT inline quotation with its source URL.

checks.label: no typed quote marks
checks.hint: The browser adds the quote marks - do not type them.

why: Typing quote marks inside <q> gives you two sets.

ask: Write a LONG quotation as its own block, with its source URL.
Mark up the TITLE of a book (not the author).
why: The cite ELEMENT holds a work's title. The cite ATTRIBUTE holds a URL.

ask: Show a snippet of program text inline.
Show a block of code keeping your exact spacing and line breaks.
why: pre is the only element that preserves your whitespace.

ask: Mark up the contact details for this page.
why: address is for CONTACT details, not any postal address.

ask: Write an HTML comment that will not appear on the page.
solution: <!-- this is a note for developers -->
why: Comments are invisible on the page but fully visible in View Source.

ask: Write an unordered list of three items.
Write an ordered list that starts counting at 3 and uses letters.
Write a description list defining two terms.
Nest a list INSIDE a list item (not between two items).

checks.label: sub-list is inside an li
checks.hint:
The inner
    must open inside an
  • , before that item's
    • .

why: A sub-list belongs to ONE item, so it lives inside that item.

ask: Write a link to an external website.

checks.label: absolute link
checks.hint: Use a full https:// address in href.

ask: Write a relative link to about.html in the same folder.
Write a link that jumps to a section of THIS page, and the heading it jumps to.

checks.label: matching id exists
checks.hint: The target needs id="contact" or the click does nothing.

why: No matching id means a silent, broken-looking link.

ask: Write a link that opens an email client.
Open a link in a new tab SAFELY.

checks.label: has noopener
checks.hint: Add rel="noopener" or the new page can control your tab.

why: Without noopener the opened page can redirect your tab to a fake login.

ask: Add an image with descriptive alt text and reserved space.

checks.label: alt is descriptive
checks.hint: alt must describe the picture in 10+ characters.

why: alt is shown when the image fails and read aloud to blind users.

ask: Make an image clickable.
Add an image with a caption, using the correct elements.
Mark up the main navigation of a site.
Write the page masthead containing the site title and its nav.
Wrap the page's unique content in the correct element.

checks.label: only one main
checks.hint: A page may contain exactly one <main>.

ask: Write a themed section WITH its own heading.

checks.label: section has a heading
checks.hint: Put a heading just inside the <section>.

why: A section with no heading was probably meant to be a div.

ask: Write a self-contained item that would make sense on another site.
Add a sidebar of related-but-not-essential content.
Close the page with a footer containing contact details.
Embed an audio file WITH working playback controls.

checks.label: audio has controls
checks.hint: Add the word controls, or nobody can press play.

checks.label: audio is closed
checks.hint: <audio> is not an empty element - close it.

ask: Embed a video with controls, a poster image, TWO source formats and fallback text.
solution:
<video width="480" controls poster="cover.jpg">
  <source src="clip.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="clip.webm" type="video/webm">
  Your browser cannot play this video.
</video>
why: The browser plays the first <source> it understands.

ask: Write a video that autoplays - correctly, so browsers allow it.

checks.label: has muted
checks.hint: autoplay is BLOCKED unless muted is also present.

why: Browsers refuse unexpected sound, so autoplay needs muted.

ask: Embed another web page, with the accessibility attribute it needs.
solution:
<iframe src="https://example.com/map" width="600" height="350"
        title="Map of the campus"></iframe>

checks.label: iframe has a title
checks.hint: Every iframe needs title="..." or a screen reader just says 'frame'.

ask: Create an SVG canvas 200px wide with a 0-100 coordinate system.
why: viewBox is the coordinate space; width is the size on screen.

ask: Draw a circle of radius 40 at the centre of a 100x100 viewBox.
solution:
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="200">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="teal"></circle>
</svg>

ask: Draw a rectangle and a straight line inside an SVG.
solution:
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="200">
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="50" height="30"></rect>
  <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="100" y2="100" stroke="black"></line>
</svg>

checks.label: line has a stroke
checks.hint: A line with no stroke is invisible.

why: A line without stroke draws nothing at all.

ask: Put text inside an SVG and give the graphic an accessible label.
solution:
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="200" role="img"
     aria-label="A badge reading CSE326">
  <text x="20" y="50">CSE326</text>
</svg>

checks.label: svg has aria-label
checks.hint: SVG has no alt - use role="img" and aria-label.

why: alt does not exist on <svg>.

ask: Build a table with a caption, a header row group and a body.
why: caption must be the first child of <table>.

ask: Add a footer row that spans all three columns.
Merge one cell ACROSS two columns.
why: A row with colspan="2" needs one FEWER cell tag.

ask: Merge one cell DOWN two rows.
why: The second row has no cell of its own in that column.

ask: Add scope attributes so a screen reader reads the table properly.
why: A cheap exam mark that almost nobody uses.

ask: Write a form that posts to /register.
Write a text field with a label tied to it AND a name so it submits.

checks.label: for matches id
checks.hint: The label's for must exactly match the input's id.

checks.label: input has name
checks.hint: Without name the value is never submitted.

why: id links the label; name is what the server receives.

ask: Write a multi-line comment box.
Write a drop-down with three choices, the second pre-selected.
Group related fields and caption the group.
why: Essential for radio groups - it names what the choice is about.

ask: Write a submit button and a reset button.
Show a task that is 70% complete.
Write an input of type text.
why: Plain single-line text.

ask: Write an input of type password.
why: Characters are hidden behind dots.

ask: Write an input of type email.
why: Browser checks the shape; phones show an @ key.

ask: Write an input of type number.
why: Digits only, with a spinner and a number pad.

ask: Write an input of type date.
why: Opens a date picker the user cannot mistype.

ask: Write an input of type time.
why: Opens a time picker.

ask: Write an input of type file.
why: Opens the file chooser.

ask: Write an input of type range.
why: A slider for approximate values.

ask: Write a number field accepting only 16 to 60, in steps of 1.
why: Validation with no JavaScript at all.

ask: Write THREE radio buttons that actually work as one group.
solution:
<label><input type="radio" name="year" value="1" checked> First</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="year" value="2"> Second</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="year" value="3"> Third</label>

checks.label: they share one name
checks.hint: All radios in a group need the SAME name, or they will not clear each other.

checks.label: one is pre-selected
checks.hint: Add checked to one of them.

why: The shared name is what makes them mutually exclusive.

ask: Write two checkboxes that submit together under one key.
solution:
<input type="checkbox" name="tags" value="web"> Web
<input type="checkbox" name="tags" value="ai" checked> AI

checks.label: they share a name
checks.hint: Give both the same name to submit as a set.

why: Unlike radios, same-named checkboxes can all be ticked.

ask: Write a field the form refuses to submit while empty.
Write a field that is visible and SUBMITTED but not editable.

checks.label: not disabled
checks.hint: disabled would NOT be submitted - readonly is correct here.

why: readonly submits; disabled does not. A favourite exam question.

ask: Write a field that is greyed out and NOT submitted.
why: A disabled field is excluded from submission entirely.

ask: Write a field with a 10-character limit and a hint inside it.
why: A placeholder is a hint, NOT a label - it vanishes when typing starts.

ask: Give an element a unique identifier and a reusable class.
why: id must be unique on the page; class can repeat.

ask: Allow a file input to accept more than one file.
Style every paragraph on the page with an element selector.

checks.label: styles p
checks.hint: Write p { color: ...; } inside a <style> block.

ask: Style anything carrying the class 'card'.

checks.label: class selector
checks.hint: Write .card { ... } - do not forget the dot.

why: Forgetting the dot makes it look for a <card> element.

ask: Style the single element whose id is 'header'.
Style only paragraphs that are INSIDE an article.

checks.label: descendant selector
checks.hint: Write article p { ... } - the space means 'inside'.

why: The space is a real operator meaning 'somewhere inside'.

ask: Style ONE element that carries both 'card' and 'wide'.

checks.label: compound selector
checks.hint: Write .card.wide with NO space between them.

why: With a space it would mean a .wide inside a .card instead.

ask: Style h1 and h2 with a single rule.
Style every input whose type is email.
Make width mean the FULL width, padding and border included.
why: One line that removes an entire category of sizing bug.

ask: Give a box 20px of space INSIDE its border and 10px outside.
why: Padding takes the background colour; margin is always transparent.

ask: Centre a fixed-width block horizontally.

checks.label: uses margin auto
checks.hint: Use margin: 0 auto; with a width set.

why: auto splits the leftover space evenly on both sides.

ask: Pin a badge to the top-right corner of a card.
solution:
<style>
  .card { position: relative; }
  .badge { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px; }
</style>
why: Without relative on the parent, the badge flies to the page corner.

ask: Make a header stay at the top when the page scrolls.

checks.label: has a top value
checks.hint: sticky silently does nothing without top: 0.

ask: Lay out a navbar: logo left, links right, vertically centred.
solution:
<style>
  .nav { display: flex; justify-content: space-between;
         align-items: center; }
</style>

ask: Make a row of cards that wraps on small screens and shares width.
solution:
<style>
  .row { display: flex; gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .row .card { flex: 1 1 220px; }
</style>

ask: Centre something perfectly, horizontally and vertically.
solution:
<style>
  .hero { display: flex; justify-content: center;
          align-items: center; height: 200px; }
</style>
why: Before Flexbox this genuinely required hacks.

ask: Build a responsive gallery with NO media query.
solution:
<style>
  .gallery { display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));
    gap: 14px; }
</style>
why: The column count changes by itself as the window resizes.

ask: Write a sidebar layout that only appears on wider screens.
why: Mobile-first: phone layout first, then ADD for bigger screens.

ask: Change a link's colour when the mouse is over it.
Give a form field a visible style when it has keyboard focus.
why: Without a focus style, keyboard users cannot tell where they are.

ask: Stripe every second row of a list.
Insert an arrow before every paragraph using a pseudo-ELEMENT.

checks.label: uses ::before
checks.hint: Use two colons for a pseudo-element: p::before.

checks.label: sets content
checks.hint: ::before does nothing without a content property.

why: One colon is a state; two colons is a part.

ask: Define a brand colour once and use it twice.
why: Change one line and the whole theme changes.

ask: Make a button's colour change smoothly on hover.

checks.label: transition on base state
checks.hint: Put transition on the NORMAL rule, not on :hover, or it snaps back.

why: On :hover only, it eases in and snaps out.

ask: Write a keyframe animation that fades an element in, and apply it.
solution:
<style>
  @keyframes fadeIn { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  .card { animation: fadeIn .4s ease both; }
</style>
